steps: 1. Read data_quality.missing_data_flags first. Resolve every flag whose `needs_analyst_research` is true by web research, citing the source and its timestamp (confirmed QB, injuries, late weather).
2. Read football.matchup_comparison and schedules.json: weigh opponent-adjusted offense vs the ACTUAL opposing defense, discount stats built on weak schedules, and do not over-weight last-3 form.
3. Read game_script: the dominant, competitive and upset scripts, and what evidence would flip each.
4. Use distributions.json for shape and spread (reference-class frequencies, closest games, the baseline's real error). Do not invent a score and assume a normal curve.

5. Write YOUR probability and an uncertainty range for each thesis you will price (winner, cover, total, team totals, halves, quarters, ladders). Keep them football-derived: never copy Kalshi's implied probability.

6. Compare every listed contract of the relevant families (markets.json) on the side you would buy, at the NO ask for NO, with the all-in cost. Use bet-up-to prices from your LOWER bound. A stake is optional, advisory and yours: leave it unsized unless you can justify it (max 5U, 1U = $75).
7. Reconcile correlated exposure across contracts and games, then return one ranked card. Passing is a correct answer.

findings.statement: New Mexico's defense out-rates the opposing offense on a down-to-down basis (-1.38 for Air Force's offense).
New Mexico holds the early-down edge: its offense stays ahead of the chains on 1st and 2nd down against this defense (-0.25) more than Air Force does (-1.74).

New Mexico owns the stronger opponent-adjusted explosive-play matchup: New Mexico offense vs Air Force defense +0.51, Air Force offense vs New Mexico defense -0.77 (explosive-play rate, opponent-adjusted: New Mexico offense #33 of 138, Air Force defense #58 of 138).
New Mexico's explosive rushing offense meets a Air Force defense that allows explosive rush plays (+1.63).

New Mexico owns the stronger opponent-adjusted scoring matchup: New Mexico offense vs Air Force defense +0.13, Air Force offense vs New Mexico defense -1.20 (points per game, opponent-adjusted: New Mexico offense #31 of 138, Air Force defense #40 of 138).

New Mexico owns the stronger opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup: New Mexico offense vs Air Force defense -0.26, Air Force offense vs New Mexico defense -1.38 (success rate, opponent-adjusted: New Mexico offense #76 of 138, Air Force defense #68 of 138).
Both offenses and both defenses point to fewer snaps than an average FBS game (possession environment -1.90).
New Mexico's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.12, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.
Air Force's leading passer in its last game (Evan Medders) is not its season leader (Liam Szarka): season passing numbers may not describe the quarterback who plays.
New Mexico's leading passer in its last game (Luke Moga) is not its season leader (Toa Fa'avae): season passing numbers may not describe the quarterback who plays.
